title: Quantitative analysis of methylation and hydroxymethylation using oXBS-qMSP
author: Hector Hernandez-Vargas
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.52bg8an
materials: Fully unmethylated DNA control Several controls are necessary to ensure your experiments are working efficiently. Whole genome amplification is sufficient to synthesize unmethylated DNA controls. We recommend the Qiagen REPLI-g whole genome amplification kit. PCR amplification should be performed according to manufacturer’s instructions.

The following link is to the detailed protocol for WGA needed to prepare a fully unmethylated sample. Starting material 1-10ng of DNA. The steps are outlined in the sub-sections to follow, however, reading the original protocol before-hand is advised. https://www.qiagen.com/fr/service-and-support/learning-hub/technologies-and-research-topics/wga/replig-principal-procedure/#REPLIg-protocols

Selecting the Primer sequences Meth Primer will suggest primer sequences for both methylated and unmethylated DNA. It is important to order both the methylated and unmethylated primers since two PCRs will be performed per sample. One for the methylated and another for the unmethylated. Once you have selected the ideal primer sequences for your experiment, the oligos can be ordered through your preferred platform such as Invitrogen and optimised for melting temp and concentration as with regular primers for qPCR.

steps.title: Design MSP Primers
steps.instruction: Identify target regions using the UCSC genome browser and design primers for methylated and unmethylated DNA using tools like MethPrimer.

substeps.instruction: Paste the FASTA record into MethPrimer and select 'Pick MSP primers'.
Set desired melting temperatures and product size (default settings are generally sufficient).
Ensure primers include at least 1 CpG site in the sequence to detect methylation.

steps.title: Prepare Fully Methylated DNA Control
steps.instruction: Methylate DNA using the enzyme SAM (S-adenosylmethionine) (ZYMO cat# E2010), ideally using unmethylated DNA synthesized in previous steps.

substeps.instruction: Set up a 20 µl reaction with: 2 µL 10X CpG Reaction Buffer, 1 µL 20X SAM (12 mM), 4 µL DNA at 100-250 ng/µl (max 1000 ng), 1 µL CpG Methylase (4 units/µl), and 12 µL Water.
Incubate at 30 °C for 4 hours.
Add an additional 1 µL 20X SAM (12 mM).
Incubate at 30 °C for another 4 hours.
Store fully methylated DNA at -20 °C.

steps.title: Amplify DNA via REPLI-g Mini
steps.instruction: Perform DNA amplification using the REPLI-g Mini system.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Buffer D1 and N1 separately.
Mix 5 µL of template with 5 µL of Buffer D1 in a microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate at room temperature for 3 minutes.
Add 10 µL of Buffer N1 and mix by vortexing.
Prepare master mix (MM) on ice by adding 1 µL REPLI-g Mini DNA Polymerase to 29 µL REPLI-g Mini reaction Buffer.
Add 30 µL of MM to the 20 µL of denatured DNA (total volume 50 µL).
Incubate at 30 °C for 16 hours.
Inactivate polymerase by heating to 65 °C for 3 minutes.
Store amplified DNA at -20 °C.

steps.title: Perform Oxidative Bisulfite Conversion
steps.instruction: Convert DNA samples using the Nugen oXBS protocol, splitting each sample into two parallel reactions: regular bisulfite conversion (BS) and oxidative bisulfite conversion (oXBS).

substeps.instruction: Process 100 ng - 1000 ng of each sample, control, or standard according to manufacturer instructions (Nugen oXBS protocol).
For controls and standards, use 1000 ng to ensure sufficient DNA for optimization.
Final volume after conversion should be 200 µL.
Store converted DNA at -20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Standard Curve for % Methylation
steps.instruction: Prepare converted DNA standards to determine primer specificity for methylated vs unmethylated DNA.

substeps.instruction: For 1 qMSP reaction, use the following volumes: 100% Methylation (FM: 10 µL, FU: 0 µL), 70% (FM: 7 µL, FU: 3 µL), 30% (FM: 3 µL, FU: 7 µL), 10% (FM: 1 µL, FU: 9 µL), 0% (FM: 0 µL, FU: 10 µL).
Alternatively, prepare serial dilutions by diluting fully methylated DNA into unmethylated DNA by a factor of 1/3 for each dilution.
Multiply volumes by the number of technical replicates and primer sets required.

steps.title: Perform qMSP Reaction
steps.instruction: Conduct quantitative Methylation-Specific PCR (qMSP) using SYBR green.

substeps.instruction: Set up 1 reaction with: 10 µL SYBR, 1 µL Forward Primer, 1 µL Reverse Primer, and 8 µL Template (use 2 µL - 8 µL of converted DNA depending on concentration).
Prepare 6x the reactions per sample (BS and oXBS in triplicate).
Run qPCR using the following stages: 1) 95 °C for 15 min, 2) 95 °C for 0.15 min, 3) 60 °C for 0.3 min (repeat steps 2-3 for 40 cycles), 4) Melt Curve from 55-95 °C in 0.5 °C increments.

steps.title: Analyze Results and Calculate Beta Values
steps.instruction: Determine the percentage of methylation and hydroxymethylation using Ct values.

substeps.instruction: Plot Ct values against log(starting concentration) for each primer set; ensure a straight line with high R2 and slope ~3.2.
Calculate M = 2^-(Ct for Methylated primers) and U = 2^-(Ct for Unmethylated primers).
Calculate Beta Value = M / (M + U).
Determine 5mC = Beta Value for oXBS.
Determine 5hmC = Beta Value for BS - Beta Value for oXBS.
